title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 45-47, 24 June 1986). Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'spécieux' (resp. 'polyédral') spaces combinatorially, as a programme of tame topology. The data are a set M of 'pieces' with an incidence order ≤, a strict 'interior' relation ≪ (ring-<), and a disjointness relation ∥. There is a distinguished subfamily L, apparently of elementary or 'linear' pieces, treated earlier around p. 22. For each X, comb_Λ(X) (Omb_Λ(X), the 'shadow' of X) is the set of pieces of Λ lying in X. The ~ notation and ∩ give the 'trace' L = X ∩ Y, and X'_L is the part of the shadow X' lying over L.

On p. 45 he generalizes the L-axioms to an arbitrary subfamily Λ ⊂ M closed under ≤:
- Λ1 (density): every X contains some Z ∈ Λ with Z ≪ X.
- Λ2: disjointness of X and Y is detected on their Λ-shadows.
- Λ3 = DΛ: a local-to-global disjointness criterion. If the shadows are disjoint over L = X ∩ Y, they are disjoint.
- CΛ*: the spec or pol variant of the criterion for X ≱ Y, with in the pol case the extra clause L = ∅ or L ∈ M.
He also lists implications among these and the 'absolute' axioms C, D, D0, C*.

This page:
1. A 'complete' set of compatibility conditions, implying all the relevant axioms C, D, C*, Λ1, Λ2, Λ3, CΛ* (and D ⇒ D0), can be chosen in several equivalent ways:
   a) Λ1, Λ2, Λ3, CΛ*
   b) Λ1, Λ2, D, C*
   c) Λ1, CΛ*, D
   d) Λ1, Λ2, C*, D0
2. The marked equivalences Λ3 ⇔ D and CΛ* ⇔ C* hold in the presence of Λ1 and Λ2. In other words, they hold when Λ is a 'très dense' part of M.
3. NB: Λ1 is the only partial axiom that occurs in every one of these systems.
4. Definition: when the conditions hold, the structure is called Λ-spécieuse, resp. Λ-polyédrale.
5. Special cases:
   - Λ = L. This is the case already treated, but it presupposes that the conditions of divisibility are satisfied automatically.
   - Λ = M. Then Λ1 is tautological, Λ2 ⇔ D0, Λ3 ⇔ D and CΛ* ⇔ C*; one gets 'M-polyèdres'. A is M-spécieux iff it satisfies D and C spec (resp. C pol).
6. Conclusion: in general, A is Λ-spécieux iff it is M-spécieux (i.e. spécieux tout court) and Λ is very dense (Λ1 + Λ2).

In short, the choice of a generating subfamily Λ does not change the class of spaces, provided Λ is very dense. This is an invariance or 'comparison' statement.

The next page (p. 47) then seeks intrinsic conditions on (M, ≤, ≪, Λ, ∥_Λ), with ∥ given only on Λ, guaranteeing that the data come from a Λ-spécieux situation. That is a reconstruction of the space from a dense sub-family.
errors: System d) (Λ1, Λ2, C*, D0) does not visibly yield D or Λ3 from the implications listed on p. 45. There, D is obtained only from Λ2+Λ3, and Λ3 only from D. One needs an extra implication, presumably of the form C* (+Λ2) + D0 ⇒ D, perhaps the analogue of a result on p. 22 that is not restated. As written on pp. 45-46, completeness of d) is therefore not justified.
Similarly, none of the systems explicitly yields C (as opposed to C*); the p. 45 diagram 'Λ3 + CΛ* ⇒ C' is only partially legible. Completeness with respect to C depends on that implication.
The final claim (Λ-spécieux ⇔ spécieux + Λ très dense) is consistent with system b): Λ1, Λ2 plus D, C*. It is a reformulation rather than a proved theorem.

ideas.what: Equivalent complete axiom systems (a)-(d) for a combinatorial 'spécieux/polyédral' structure relative to a subfamily Λ; Λ1 (density) is common to all.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatics of tame/stratified spaces via a generating family of cells; equivalence of axiom systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct analogue; tame topology later developed as o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only calls for a tame topology, without such axiomatics

ideas.what: Notion of a 'très dense' subfamily Λ (Λ1 + Λ2): every piece contains interior Λ-pieces, and disjointness is detected on Λ-shadows.
ideas.modern_name: Dense generating sub-family / basis; analogous to a dense subsite
ideas.usually_credited_to: Comparison lemma for dense subsites: SGA 4 (Grothendieck–Verdier)
ideas.where_published: Analogy only: SGA 4 Exp. III comparison lemma

ideas.what: Invariance statement: Λ-spécieux ⇔ spécieux (M-spécieux) + Λ very dense; the special cases Λ = L and Λ = M.
ideas.modern_name: Independence of a structure from the choice of a dense generating family

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 combinatorial axiomatization of 'spécieux' and 'polyédral' spaces is an attempt at the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. It uses pieces with relations ≤, ≪, ∥ and dense generating subfamilies Λ, and is distinct from o-minimality. This page fixes the equivalent axiom systems and the invariance under change of a very dense Λ. The framework is little studied in the literature.
missed.quote: Dans le cas général, on peut dire que A est (...) Λ-spécieux, ssi il est M-spécieux i.e. spécieux tout court, et si de plus Λ est très dense (Λ1 et Λ2)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a purely combinatorial or order-theoretic axiomatics of tame spaces, built from cells and disjointness relations. This could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions, regular CW posets, or exit-path/stratified approaches. The thread was never developed in print.

missed.claim: The invariance under change of very dense Λ is formally analogous to the SGA 4 comparison lemma (dense subsites give the same topos), transplanted to tame topology. Grothendieck does not state the analogy here; it is implicit.
missed.quote: les équivalences marquées valent (...) en présence de Λ1, Λ2 i.e. si Λ est partie très dense de M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests treating tame spaces site-theoretically, with generating families of cells as dense subsites. This is a perspective seldom made explicit in o-minimal or stratified-space literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mainly technical bookkeeping of equivalent axiom systems in an unpublished framework. The framework itself (combinatorial tame topology, 1986) is little known, but this page contains no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: 'C sup resp. C pol' should read 'C spéc resp. C pol' (spécieux vs polyédral variants).
'on [?] M-polyèdres' likely reads 'en M-polyèdres' / 'ou M-polyèdres', paralleling 'Λ-spécieuse, ou Λ-polyédrale'.
In item d) the third symbol is overwritten (C* written over another letter); the reading Λ1, Λ2, C*, D0 is plausible.
'valent toujours [?] à tendance [?]' is uncertain; the sense is 'valent (au moins) en présence de Λ1, Λ2'.
Next page 'Omb_Λ' and previous page 'comb_Λ' denote the same operator (likely 'Omb' = ombre/shadow).
